planner_capacity_policy.target_immediately_eligible_unclaimed: >=10 when legitimate dependencies and scope permit
planner_capacity_policy.current_priority: Current and earlier unresolved active work always outranks dependency-blocked future work.
planner_capacity_policy.future_predecomposition: README/ROADMAP-defined near-future work may be pre-decomposed only when useful for capacity and must remain explicitly blocked until its phase/dependencies are eligible.
planner_capacity_policy.parallelism: Maintain useful Coder and Designer parallelism when legitimate approved work permits.
planner_capacity_policy.anti_filler: Never invent features/gameplay, duplicate existing scope, split into artificial micro-tasks, or create filler merely to satisfy an issue-count target. If fewer legitimate issues exist, keep the truthful lower count.

core_rule: Player advises -> AI Character decides -> Simulation validates -> World reacts.

baseline.public_policy: The stable public URL may serve an Admin-directed unverified development build when explicitly authorized. Normal independently verified status requires an independent Tester; an otherwise-ready cumulative phase/release gate may instead advance through an accurately labeled DEADLOCK TESTER PASS when the README-defined all-identities Tester deadlock conditions are satisfied.

phase_policy.origin_rule: Every new campaign begins at authoritative world coordinate (0,0) in the SEED-generated inhabited starting village, with the initial playable view centered on the campaign origin.
phase_policy.map_rule: Every cumulative phase must preserve and progressively extend the persistent living strategic world map as the primary playable surface. The visible tile region is only a local active part of the larger continuous world, not a finite complete map.
phase_policy.world_generation_rule: Compatible SEED + world coordinates + compatible generator rules reproduce the same unmodified base world. Base composition includes coherent terrain/water/roads/bridges, settlement archetype foundations, local populations, habitat/ecology foundations and, where political organization applies, coherent base realm/country, region/province, territorial/border relationships and settlement-affiliation identity. Neighboring regions remain deterministic and available without a gameplay-defined outer boundary.
phase_policy.political_geography_rule: The SEED defines reproducible base political geography as part of the same physical world rather than disconnected labels: realm/country and region/province identity, settlement affiliation and territorial relationships should be spatially coherent with terrain, water, routes, settlements and neighboring regions. Campaign history may later change ownership, borders, affiliations, capitals or realm composition; those authoritative changes refine/override the unchanged base without rewriting the SEED.
phase_policy.settlement_evolution_rule: Settlements have authoritative historical development state rather than frozen templates. Campaign time and simulation outcomes may support stability, growth, contraction, damage, recovery, fortification, functional change, abandonment, ruin or repopulation. Detailed materialization must reflect accumulated development state instead of silently resetting to the untouched SEED template.
phase_policy.persistence_rule: Deterministic unchanged base-world content, including unchanged base political geography, may be regenerated from SEED and coordinates; authoritative campaign changes are persisted. Current-world reconstruction composes SEED base state, authoritative fantasy campaign date/time, applicable hierarchical/off-screen progression including settlement development and political history, and saved persistent changes.
phase_policy.real_time_rule: The campaign is real-time rather than turn-based. At normal speed 60 real-world minutes equal one 24-hour in-game day, so one in-game hour equals 2.5 real-world minutes.
phase_policy.calendar_origin_rule: A new campaign fantasy chronology is initialized from accepted real-world civil date/time at creation: fantasy day and month numbers and time-of-day equal the real-world origin, while fantasy year = real-world year - 2000. Example: 28.08.2026 14:30 -> 28.08.0026 14:30. The initial game time is therefore not fixed at 06:00.
phase_policy.calendar_continuity_rule: The real-world creation mapping is only the synchronization origin. After creation, fantasy campaign chronology remains its own accelerated authoritative timeline and must not be directly remapped to current civil date/time on launch. Accepted real-world elapsed time advances that established chronology at normal speed: one real-world hour = one in-game day, 24 real hours = 24 in-game days, and 10 real days = 240 in-game days, using bounded catch-up rather than replaying every missed tick.
phase_policy.day_night_rule: Authoritative game time defines dawn/daylight transition at 05:00 and darkness/night transition at 22:00. Moving physically accurate shadows are not required.
phase_policy.simulation_fidelity_rule: The protagonist's active/relevant region uses continuous high-detail simulation; nearby relevant state may use reduced-frequency or aggregate processing; far inactive/unloaded detail should normally perform no continuous entity-level ticking and instead use lower-cost authoritative derivation or elapsed-time reconciliation when required.
phase_policy.hierarchical_simulation_rule: The same authoritative world may be represented at progressively different resolution from global/world through realm/country, region, settlement and local active layers. Compact higher-level state preserves large-scale causality, settlement-development history and political/territorial state without materializing all local entities.
phase_policy.relevance_bounded_simulation_rule: Invisible-world computation scales with relevance and authoritative information required, not total generated, discovered or theoretically unbounded world size. Irrelevant local detail remains unticked where possible; long elapsed periods use bounded aggregate/end-state reconciliation rather than replaying every missed local action or tick.
phase_policy.asynchronous_determinism_rule: Expensive generation, catch-up, refinement and materialization should be asynchronous-capable where practical so unrelated distant work does not block interactive play. Scheduling, completion order, render order, visit order, device speed, synchronous/asynchronous execution and stale job timing must not change authoritative results; late/stale results cannot overwrite newer authoritative state.
phase_policy.lazy_materialization_rule: Unvisited or inactive detailed state is materialized only when relevant from compatible SEED base state, coordinates, authoritative fantasy campaign date/time, accumulated hierarchical outcomes including settlement-development and political-geography history, meaningful events, persistent changes and local rules; visit/render/scheduling order must not become authority.
phase_policy.device_performance_rule: Current desktop browsers, phones and tablets are gameplay targets. Presentation quality and non-authoritative fidelity may scale to device capability, while simulation correctness, chronology, legal outcomes, persistence and deterministic world reconstruction remain unchanged. Performance validation must include representative mobile/tablet conditions before final release.
phase_policy.character_art_direction_rule: Character presentation converges toward an original seinen-anime-inspired language: mature believable proportions, grounded readable silhouettes, restrained but expressive emotion, clear age/status/profession/culture distinction and plausible medieval-fantasy clothing/material wear. It must not copy a specific existing artist, series, protected character, costume, composition or signature style.
phase_policy.old_school_rpg_visual_rule: World and interface presentation should evoke old-school PC RPGs through isometric/near-isometric composition, painterly/hand-crafted or pre-rendered-feeling depth, grounded materials/palette, restrained effects, atmosphere and classic RPG information framing while retaining modern accessibility, responsive layouts and mobile/tablet performance.
phase_policy.visual_cohesion_rule: Portraits, in-world characters, creatures, environments, settlements, UI ornament and later strategic-scale views should read as one coherent product family. Placeholder assets may remain during development but later replacement/final art must converge toward the README visual direction.
phase_policy.strategic_scale_view_rule: As protagonist authority expands, regional, realm/country and wider-world strategic views must summarize authoritative aggregate state and evolving political geography from the same living world rather than create disconnected dashboard truth.
phase_policy.npc_life_rule: NPC routines may be time-aware and role/location dependent; simple varied deterministic/Local-BOT ambient NPC-to-NPC dialogue may respond to profession, settlement/location, environment, time and relevant local conditions without becoming authoritative truth by itself.
phase_policy.ecology_rule: Domestic/farm animals, wildlife and a broad original medieval-fantasy bestiary are SEED/habitat/context-aware simulation-backed world content where gameplay-relevant.
phase_policy.designer_rule: Every phase requires at least one independently testable Designer-role task before normal phase completion. After README visual-direction changes, the earliest relevant active phase must establish or reconcile a compatible visual-direction foundation rather than relying only on unrelated previously verified placeholder work.
phase_policy.tester_deadlock_rule: Normal phase/release verification uses an independent Worker acting as Tester. If an otherwise-ready cumulative gate has no authorized independent Tester because every available Worker identity has accepted authorship inside the gate scope, and no unresolved revision/dependency/claim/higher-authority blocker remains, the first Worker whose authorized turn reaches the Tester gate may perform the full exact-state verification and issue an accurately labeled DEADLOCK TESTER PASS. That PASS is sufficient to advance the phase/release but must not be represented as independent verification of that Worker's own included work.
phase_policy.normal_phase_transition_rule: Under normal autonomous progression, an independent Worker acting in the Tester role passes the active phase gate before the next phase activates. The Tester must not approve work produced by the same Worker identity unless the README-defined all-identities Tester deadlock exception applies. Under that exception, the first Worker whose authorized turn reaches the otherwise-ready gate may complete all required verification and issue DEADLOCK TESTER PASS, which is valid phase/release authority with accurate independence attribution. Explicit Admin instructions may separately override publication or phase/release workflow requirements.
